subject: Lavaan version 0.6-19 - Robust values not being calculated for multigroup CFA

messages.author: 6fc96e6b7d1c361e
messages.subject: Lavaan version 0.6-19 - Robust values not being calculated for multigroup CFA
parts:
I'm currently running a confirmatory factor analysis using a higher-order model with two sets of variables in a sample including 3 groups. The original model is able to run and shows acceptable fit values. However, when trying to run the multi-group CFA (specifying the group variable), the robust fit statistics are NA. 

This is how I'm specifying the function:
NCSC_CFA_himodel_gr_fit <- cfa(NCSC_CFA_himodel, data = himodel_df, group="group",std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml")

Here is the warning message I received:

Warning: lavaan->lav_fit_cfi_lavobject():  
   computation of robust CFI failed.Warning: lavaan->lav_fit_rmsea_lavobject():  
   computation of robust RMSEA failed.

Please let me know how I can resolve this issue as I need the robust values to compute measurement invariance testing.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan version 0.6-19 - Robust values not being calculated for multigroup CFA
parts:
You have not provided enough information to diagnose the problem.  Try providing a reprex

https://or.meta.stackexchange.com/questions/191/what-is-a-minimal-reproducible-example-reprex-and-how-do-i-write-one

For example, the robust test statistics are not missing in this reprex:

dat1 <- lavaan::HolzingerSwineford1939
set.seed(12345)
dat1$z <- rnorm(nrow(dat1))
dat1$x5 <- ifelse(dat1$z < quantile(dat1$z, .3), NA, dat1$x5)
dat1$x9 <- ifelse(dat1$z > quantile(dat1$z, .8), NA, dat1$x9)

mod <- "
  visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
  textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
  speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9
"
fit <- cfa(mod, data = dat1, group = "school", std.lv = TRUE,
estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml")

summary(fit, fit.measures = TRUE)

So it is probably necessary to provide at least some of your data (along with an R script that produces the output you refer to, not just your cfa() call) for anyone to track down your specific issue.

messages.subject: Re: Lavaan version 0.6-19 - Robust values not being calculated for multigroup CFA
parts:
Hi Ayesha, 

I ran your reprex and the problem seems to stem from Group A. 

If you run:
summary(NCSC_CFA_himodel_gr_fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

for the model in the reprex and look at the NC =~LG and SC =~sim estimates in the output, you will see that these estimates (and their associated standard errors) are unrealistically high compared to other estimates in the model. Although the model seems to have converged (NCSC_CFA_himodel_gr_fit@optim$converged), it looks like there were some problems with the estimation. Pasting only the relevant part of the output below:

Group 1 [A]:

Latent Variables:

                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all

  NC =~                                                                 

    PS                1.772    0.993    1.786    0.074    0.871    0.871

    AWM               1.187    0.333    3.567    0.000    0.765    0.765

    LG               98.227   35.403    2.775    0.006    1.000    1.000

  SC =~                                                                 

    sim              82.090   39.173    2.096    0.036    1.000    1.000

    ment              0.999    0.316    3.163    0.002    0.707    0.707


If you fit a multigroup model only for data from groups B and C, all robust fit measures (including the CFI and RMSEA) are computed as expected: 

# run model WITHOUT group A included

NCSC_CFA_himodel_grBC_fit <- cfa(NCSC_CFA_himodel, data = himodel_df[himodel_df$group != "A",], 

                                 group="group", std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml")


summary(NCSC_CFA_himodel_grBC_fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)

However, if you fit a single-group model only for Group A, model estimation fails and no fit measures are computed (also, estimates for NC =~LG and SC =~sim are unrealistically high):

# run single-group model ONLY with group A

NCSC_CFA_himodel_grA_fit <- cfa(NCSC_CFA_himodel, data = himodel_df[himodel_df$group == "A",],
std.lv = TRUE, estimator = "MLR", missing = "ml")

Warning message:

lavaan->lav_lavaan_step11_estoptim():  

   Model estimation FAILED! Returning starting values. 


summary(NCSC_CFA_himodel_grA_fit, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized=TRUE, rsquare=TRUE)


Warning message:

lavaan->lav_object_summary():  

   fit measures not available if model did not converge


My guess is that this is due to a small sample size within Group A (110 people) relative to the model size (54 parameters). I would also check whether the same factor structure applies across groups. 


I hope this helps!

Aditi

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Lavaan version 0.6-19 - Robust values not being calculated for multigroup CFA
parts:
On 3/26/25 6:43 PM, Ayesha Rashidi wrote:
> If we set std.lv =
> FALSE or bounds = 'standard' for the current higher order model, do the
> nested models need to be re-run using the same syntax?
Preferably, yes.

> Additionally, is
> there a more appropriate solution between the two i.e. std.lv=FALSE or
> bounds='standard'?

If it works with std.lv = FALSE, that is to be preferred. It simply
changes the way we set the metric of the latent variables, and that is a
harmless operation. You can always report the standardized solution
afterwards.

The argument bounds = "standard" potentially affects several (free)
parameters. It forces the parameters to stay between pre-specified
upper/lower bounds, in order to facilitate convergence. I would argue
that it still results in a useful solution, even if one or more
parameters are estimated at the boundary.

A paper about this 'bounded estimation' can be found here:

https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/10705511.2021.1982716

Yves.
